evidence: Nas grew up in the Queensbridge Houses. He has recalled in interview that Marley Marl and the Juice Crew gave young rappers like him hope that there was a life beyond their neighbourhood (quoted in Wikipedia's Juice Crew article). His 1994 debut 'Illmatic' is set largely in Queensbridge. The documented part is Nas's own account of the crew as an example; any specific musical debt is not claimed here.

trackPair.whatToListenFor: Start with 'The Bridge': a sampled drum break chopped and retriggered, with a lot of empty space around MC Shan's voice while he names the projects. Then play 'Memory Lane', produced by DJ Premier eight years later. The drums are still lifted from old records and still hit hard, but now there is a looped jazz sample running underneath and scratched vocal fragments on the hook. The neighbourhood is the same and so is the idea of building a beat out of other records. What changed is how much music the producers could fit around the rapper.

explanation.age13: Nas grew up in Queensbridge, the same housing project where Marley Marl made records for the Juice Crew. He has said that seeing them succeed showed kids like him that there was a life outside the neighbourhood. When his first album 'Illmatic' came out in 1994, Queensbridge was all over it.
explanation.adult: The edge runs from the scene rather than from any one producer because Nas's own account credits the collective: the Juice Crew was proof, for a teenager in the same projects, that rap could be a way out. 'Illmatic' then made Queensbridge a subject of its own, eight years after the Bridge Wars had cast it as the losing side of a borough argument. No producer on 'Illmatic' came from the Juice Crew, so the edge claims example and setting, not sound.
